questions.stem: On a Canadian metric chart, a depth is shown as 4. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: Metric chart depths are in metres below chart datum, which in BC tidal waters is a very low tide level.

questions.stem: The chart shows 2 m at a spot. The tide table gives a height of tide of 3 m. About how deep is the water there?
questions.explanation: Depth of water = charted depth + height of tide: 2 m + 3 m = 5 m.

questions.stem: Why is there usually more water than the chart shows in BC tidal waters?
options: Chart datum is a very low tide
Charts are always several years old
Depths are given in feet, not metres
The chart ignores the summer rains
questions.explanation: Chart datum is a very low tide level, so most of the time the tide adds water. On a very low tide there can be less.

questions.stem: On a chart you see a rock marked with an underlined 1. What does this tell you?
options: It is 1 m deep at all tides
It is 1 m high at high tide
questions.explanation: An underlined figure is a drying height: the rock stands 1 m above chart datum and uncovers at low tide.

questions.stem: Which 7 m pleasure craft does NOT need to carry a magnetic compass?
options: One always in sight of seamarks
One on an overnight trip offshore
One with a working GPS chartplotter
One used only on summer weekends
questions.explanation: A craft of 8 m or under that navigates within sight of seamarks is exempt. A GPS does not replace the compass.

questions.stem: Why should you keep paper charts on board if you have a GPS chartplotter?
options: The law bans plotters near shore
questions.explanation: Batteries and electronics can fail. Paper charts are the backup.

questions.stem: How many high tides does most of the BC coast get in a day?
questions.explanation: Most of the BC coast has two high and two low tides a day, and they are usually of different heights.

questions.stem: It is August. The tide table shows high water at 0940. What time is that on your watch?
questions.explanation: Canadian tide and current tables use standard time. Add one hour for daylight saving time.

options: Always the exact moment of high tide
The lowest tide of the year
Water that is sheltered from the wind
When the current stops and turns
questions.explanation: Slack water is when the tidal current stops and turns. It does not always happen at high or low water.

questions.stem: Which wind speed range is covered by a gale warning?
questions.explanation: Gale 34 to 47 knots. Strong wind is 20 to 33, storm 48 to 63, hurricane force 64 or more.

questions.stem: Environment Canada issues a strong wind warning for your area. What wind speed is expected?
questions.explanation: A strong wind warning is for 20 to 33 knots. That is dangerous for small boats.

questions.stem: The marine forecast says "wind southeast 15 knots". What does it mean?
options: Gusting to 15 knots from the east
questions.explanation: Forecast wind direction is where the wind comes from, and speed is in knots.

questions.stem: Your barometer has been falling steadily all morning. What does it suggest?
options: A high and fine weather are coming
A low or front is coming
The tide is about to turn
questions.explanation: A falling barometer warns of an approaching low or front and worse weather.

questions.stem: When are the waves in a pass usually worst?
options: When wind and current go the same way
At slack water with light winds
Just after a high tide on a calm day
When wind blows against the current
questions.explanation: Wind against current makes short, steep, breaking waves. Cross at slack or when wind and current agree.
